# PassionCode.ai

> A toolkit for AI-native teams: an open-source workplace for AI agents. Fabric is the home for your projects and their agents (early preview); Fabric Switchboard, Fabric Dashboards, Fabric Inbox and Project Observatory are its tools, and each works on its own. Everything is open source under the GNU AGPL-3.0 and free to use; a commercial license and setup for organizations (PassionCode for Enterprise) are available.

An agent you set up works for a week, then falls apart: it runs on the wrong account or hits a limit, forgets what it learned, nobody can say what it changed, and the next agent starts from zero. PassionCode.ai is a local, open-source workspace for working with AI agents, on top of Claude Code, Codex and what comes next, on the subscription you already have. You start from one command and your coding agent; the home page's How it works (https://passioncode.ai/#how) shows six steps (enter, onboard, first agent, grow, work together and watch, organization), each marked available now, preview or direction. Founders: Sergey Sheleg (co-founder and CPO of Nicegram, co-founder of eSIM Plus) and Serge Khurs (co-founder and CTO of Teslasuit), who built this setup for their own teams; their story, told by Sergey in the first person, is at https://passioncode.ai/#about.

## Vision
- [Vision](https://passioncode.ai/vision/): what holds an agent together over time (the page that defines "harness") and its four parts; four principles (projects are the axis; the work improves itself — evidence today, retrospectives as the direction; vendor-neutral, local first, open source; analytics, never surveillance); the path in six stages (one agent, two that talk, a chain, agents kept in good order, a team, an organization) each marked available now or direction; task-pipeline (github.com/ssheleg/sshlg-skills) as a recommended separate open-source skill.

## Languages
- Every page is published in English and in 9 more languages, at the same path under the language's prefix: Russian (Русский) under /ru/ — for example https://passioncode.ai/ru/start/; German (Deutsch) under /de/ — for example https://passioncode.ai/de/start/; French (Français) under /fr/ — for example https://passioncode.ai/fr/start/; Polish (Polski) under /pl/ — for example https://passioncode.ai/pl/start/; Korean (한국어) under /ko/ — for example https://passioncode.ai/ko/start/; Spanish (Español) under /es/ — for example https://passioncode.ai/es/start/; Brazilian Portuguese (Português (Brasil)) under /pt-br/ — for example https://passioncode.ai/pt-br/start/; Chinese (Simplified) (简体中文) under /zh-hans/ — for example https://passioncode.ai/zh-hans/start/; Japanese (日本語) under /ja/ — for example https://passioncode.ai/ja/start/. Each page names all its versions with hreflang, English as x-default, and sitemap.xml lists every version. English is the source; where a translated privacy notice differs, the English version prevails.

## Start
- [Get started](https://passioncode.ai/start/): install the skills (`npx @passioncode-ai/passioncode@latest update`), add Fabric (a separate preview download; its first screen offers four actions: create an agent, adapt one, open a project, create one), create or adapt an agent, run it in Fabric Dashboards, add the next agent to the same project, contribute.
- [Current releases as JSON](https://passioncode.ai/api/releases): every product's current version, release notes link, download URLs and SHA-256, resolved from GitHub releases.

## Products
- [Fabric](https://passioncode.ai/fabric/): the home for your projects and their agents, built toward acting as the CEO of your agents; early preview for macOS on Apple silicon and Intel (one universal DMG since 0.3.4); keeps each project's purpose, board, decisions and releases. Its conversation does not reply yet.
- [Coding agents Fabric works with](https://passioncode.ai/fabric/agents/): which agents Fabric connects (Claude Code, Kilo Code and Hermes Agent, as of Fabric 0.3.2), which run in it (Codex, Cline), which are planned.
- [Fabric Switchboard](https://passioncode.ai/switchboard/): local account manager for Claude Code and Codex CLI, macOS and Windows (Authenticode-signed since 0.6.16), with an MCP server (`switchboard mcp`); updates itself.
- [Switchboard agents](https://passioncode.ai/switchboard/agents/): 30 other coding agents (Hermes, Kilo Code, Cline, Goose …) get Switchboard's tools; those that accept a custom endpoint have their API-key accounts switched through it.
- [Fabric Dashboards](https://passioncode.ai/dashboards/): one window for local agent services that speak fabric-service/0.1, their state, spend and limits (Spend page), an agent console beside each dashboard; driven over MCP. macOS, Windows (signed installer, x64 and arm64) and Linux (AppImage and .deb, x64 and arm64) since 0.7.1; self-updates on macOS only, on Windows and Linux install the next release by hand.
- [Project Observatory](https://passioncode.ai/observatory/): a local dashboard of project activity and findings with evidence; CLI, MCP and dashboard; macOS, Linux and Windows (Python 3.13+). A desktop app for each: the Mac app, and since 0.22.0 a signed Windows installer and a Linux AppImage and .deb (x64 and arm64); each needs the engine installed first.
- [Fabric Inbox](https://passioncode.ai/inbox/): desktop mail for Gmail and Cloudflare mailboxes with agent reply policies, in English or Russian, with recoverable Discarded mail and discard rules (0.12.0); since 0.15 your coding agent (Claude Code or Codex) can set it up and connect once you allow it, and works in a console beside the mail (from 0.15.1; not in the Mac App Store version); development preview for macOS, Windows (Authenticode-signed installer since 0.14.1) and Linux (AppImage and .deb), x64 and arm64.
- [Fabric Agent Adapter](https://github.com/passioncode-ai/fabric-agent-adapter): skills, kits and a conformance probe that make any agent, MCP server or CLI a Fabric-compatible service.

## Organizations
- [For organizations — PassionCode for Enterprise](https://passioncode.ai/business/): making an organization AI-native, designed for 1 to 1000 people. PassionCode for Enterprise (in development, offered on request; pilots run on the open-source tools today): machines onboarded into the organization, agents rolled out, routing between agents on different machines, model access through each machine's own local agent (keys never leave the machine), activity and usage analytics, administration, custom builds signed by PassionCode.ai; data stays on your machines or your own cloud. For finance and engineering: one view of what each agent cost and what it delivered — spend per agent (Fabric Dashboards), subscription usage per account (Switchboard) and what changed per project (Observatory) available now; cost and result joined per project and workflow, and limits set once and checked by agents, are direction; about agents and workflows, never a ranking of people. Estimate = hours a week × 4.33 × share agents take (10–50% by how the work runs today) × loaded hourly cost. To request it: a short form (what agents should do, a work email, an optional goal), or let a coding agent ask.
- [Agent request prompt](https://passioncode.ai/business/agent-request.txt): plain text for a coding agent acting for a person. It asks the person a few questions one at a time, never includes code, secrets, paths, customer data or third parties' names, gets a form token (`GET https://passioncode.ai/api/leads/token`), checks the request with `POST https://passioncode.ai/api/leads?dry_run=1`, shows the final JSON and sends it to `POST https://passioncode.ai/api/leads` only after the person says yes, once, with one idempotency `id`. The same prompt in each language at /<code>/business/agent-request.txt.
- Contact: commercial@passioncode.ai
